questions.q: A graph uses core NAG at 5. What value gives the same strength in sd-perturbed-attention's NAG?
questions.why: Core's weight on the difference is φ − 1, and that pack's is φ. That matches the strength in the formula only: the two hook into different attention.

questions.q: What μ in flux_time_shift, with σ = 1, matches SD3-style shift 3?
questions.why: The second formula equals the first when α = e^μ.

questions.q: Our render of the sampler named ddim matched euler pixel for pixel. Why?
options: In core the name ddim runs euler with one inpaint option
Every sampler gives the same picture
ddim and euler share a seed list
questions.answer: In core the name ddim runs euler with one inpaint option
questions.why: That's in samplers.py. It's the name that misleads.

questions.q: What does denoise 0.5 at 20 steps do in AlignYourSteps, compared with BasicScheduler?
options: AYS runs 10 steps, and BasicScheduler still runs 20
questions.answer: AYS runs 10 steps, and BasicScheduler still runs 20
questions.why: One cuts the count, and the other samples from a longer schedule.

questions.q: Two nodes share a name but use different formulas. What can you conclude?
options: Nothing about bugs until you check what each author meant
questions.answer: Nothing about bugs until you check what each author meant
questions.why: A difference isn't a bug on its own.

questions.q: How do you compare two same-named nodes?
options: Find the formula in each and simplify them side by side
Render one seed with each and pick
questions.answer: Find the formula in each and simplify them side by side
questions.why: Tooltips and single renders can mislead.
